content: Several companies are currently manufacturing and selling electronic versions of cigarettes, commonly referred to as e-cigarettes. These devices are designed to resemble a small rod, slightly longer than a traditional cigarette. The mouthpiece of the e-cigarette contains a replaceable cartridge filled with a liquid solution. This liquid typically consists of nicotine and propylene glycol as its primary components. When the user inhales, the airflow is detected by a microprocessor within the device. The microprocessor activates an atomizer, which disperses tiny droplets of the liquid into the flowing air. This process generates a vapor mist that the user inhales. The inclusion of propylene glycol in the liquid enhances the visual resemblance of the vapor to the smoke produced by conventional cigarettes. Additionally, the microprocessor activates an orange LED at the tip of the device to simulate the appearance of a lit cigarette. The device not only mimics the visual and sensory aspects of smoking but also replicates the temperature of traditional cigarette smoke, which ranges between 50°C and 60°C. The e-cigarette operates using a rechargeable battery as its power source. The technology behind this device is protected under European Patent EP 1618803 A1. Nicotine Solution Cartridges The patent outlines four distinct formulations for the nicotine solution used in the cartridges of e-cigarettes. These formulations are designed to deliver nicotine to the user in a controlled manner. Health Issues E-cigarettes are marketed as a healthier alternative to traditional tobacco consumption, particularly when compared to smoking. This is because the atomization process used in e-cigarettes does not produce the particulate matter that results from the combustion of plant material in conventional cigarettes. A toxicity study on the nicotine solutions used in e-cigarettes has been conducted by Prof. Dr. Bernd Mayer, with the findings published in German. Legal Situation in the European Union Within the European Union, the legal status of e-cigarette products varies by country. In principle, e-cigarettes are classified as Class IIa medical devices under the EC Directive 93/42/EEC. They are intended to administer medicinal substances, such as nicotine solutions, to the human body. The nicotine cartridges are considered medicinal products under EC Directive 2001/83/EG, as the nicotine is presented in solution form rather than as a tobacco plant product. Based on this classification, all e-cigarette products must obtain CE marking before distribution. Additionally, the nicotine cartridges require registration as medicinal products prior to trade and distribution. The Austrian Agency for Healthcare Safety issued a decision on April 18, 2007, supporting this expert opinion. Since this decision was made by a competent authority in one EU country, it serves as a guideline for other EU member states. However, as of now, no e-cigarette products have successfully obtained the necessary medical device certification or medicinal product registration. Consequently, the distribution of e-cigarettes within the European Union appears to be illegal.
